review_notes: I read all of Kernel.lean. I also read the related simp-relevant declarations in Grid.lean (`stage_apply_same`, `stage_apply_ne`, `uniform_apply`, `map_apply`, `sum_mass`, `binaryLayer`). The existing simp attributes mostly look sound: `pathBetween_zero/last/input/output`, `binaryBoundary_zero/last`, `binaryPath_zero/last` and `binaryLayer_apply_same` are all terminating, oriented sensibly and have no obvious competitors. The conditional lemmas `pathBetween_step` and `binaryLayer_apply_ne` are reasonably left non-simp because they have side conditions. I found no rewrite cycles. The two findings are missing apply/unfolding lemmas for wrapper definitions (`pathLine`/`binaryPathLine`, and `endpointWeight`). Each is shown by repeated manual `change` or `convert … congr!` steps in this file. I cannot run Lean, so I don't claim the proposed lemmas make those exact steps go through. I also noticed the many `convert … using 1 <;> congr!` steps next to the local `Classical.propDecidable` instance. That may be a decidable-instance mismatch, but I couldn't confirm the cause without Lean, so I didn't report it.

findings.excerpt: def pathLine (x y : G.Slot) (j : Fin G.b) : G.Line j :=
findings.problem: `pathLine` is a bare lambda wrapper over `pathBetween ... j.castSucc`, with no apply lemma and no folding lemma. `stage_apply_same` (simp) rewrites `G.stage ω j x j` to `ω j (fun k => x k) (x j)`. For `x = pathBetween x y j.castSucc` the argument of `ω j` is therefore the expanded lambda, not `G.pathLine x y j`, so simp cannot connect the two forms. The proofs bridge the gap by hand with `change` statements that spell out the lambda (lines 296 and 314). The same happens for `binaryPathLine`, whose `fun k => if k.val.val < j.val then y k else x k` is written out in `change` at lines 528 and 547. Since `binaryPathLine` is defined through `binaryPath`, the ite form the proofs `change` to only appears after unfolding both definitions.
findings.proposed_change: Add simp lemmas that give one canonical form. For example, `pathLine_apply : G.pathLine x y j k = G.pathBetween x y j.castSucc k := rfl`, and a folding lemma `(fun k : {k // k ≠ j} => G.pathBetween x y j.castSucc k) = G.pathLine x y j := rfl`, orienting the fold so that `ω j (…)` after `stage_apply_same` lands in `pathLine` form. Do the same for `binaryPathLine` (`binaryPathLine_apply : binaryPathLine x y j k = if k.val.val < j.val then y k else x k`, or its `binaryPath` form). Then the `change` steps at 296, 314, 528 and 547 can be replaced by `simpa [pathLine_apply, …]` or `simp only`.
findings.benefit: The two direction proofs of `sweep_eq_iff_line_assignments` and `binarySweep_eq_iff_coins` no longer depend on brittle manual `change` of lambda terms. Downstream files that use `pathLine` can then normalize expressions with `simp` instead of unfolding by hand.

findings.excerpt: def endpointWeight (p : G.Slot × G.Slot) : ℝ := FiniteLaw.uniform _ p
findings.problem: `endpointWeight` is a plain def over `FiniteLaw.uniform`, and `FiniteLaw.uniform_apply` is `@[simp]`, but it can't fire because `endpointWeight` is not reducible and has no simp lemma of its own. `probability_path_vertex` and `probability_path_line` need to replace `G.endpointWeight p` by `(Fintype.card (G.Slot × G.Slot) : ℝ)⁻¹` inside a sum over an ite. They do this through `convert hs using 1; congr!` (lines 758–759 and 778–779) instead of a rewrite. The identical `convert … congr!` pattern recurs in `probability_lineShares_le` and `probability_vertexShares_le`, which also pass through `endpointWeight`. This is opaque and fragile.
findings.proposed_change: Add `theorem endpointWeight_apply (p : G.Slot × G.Slot) : G.endpointWeight p = (Fintype.card (G.Slot × G.Slot) : ℝ)⁻¹ := rfl`. Mark it `@[simp]` (mirroring `uniform_apply`) or use it via `simp only [endpointWeight_apply]`. Then replace the `convert hs using 1; congr!` steps by `simp only [endpointWeight_apply]` followed by `exact hs`, or the equivalent. The rewrite direction is safe because the RHS contains no `endpointWeight`.
findings.benefit: The calc steps in `probability_path_vertex` and `probability_path_line` become transparent rewrites. Other users of `endpointWeight` get a canonical numeric normal form instead of having to unfold the def.
